evidence_checks.notes: Quote ("交易總金額為美金48,850仟元") is verbatim in src:wistron-mops-2025-05-13-wius-contract, but that filing names only the counterparty (PR III/CROW BUILDING E,F,G&L LP) and the amount; it does not name 15200 Heritage Parkway, D1, Fort Worth, or give a land/building size. It references an original announcement dated 2025-04-02 that is not in this file's sources[]. The filing does not support this transaction being the D1/Heritage Parkway acquisition -- that link is the analyst's inference from timing and rough proportionality to the other (Westport) transaction. See fin:wistron-heritage-parkway-2025.

Quote is verbatim and does genuinely support 'segment scale' as labeled (company-wide CCS segment revenue). Flagging separately: the facility's products[] field ("networking switches", "data center racks", "servers (CCS segment)") is a company/segment-wide characterization drawn from this same passage, not a Texas-site-specific disclosure -- the 10-K property table gives no product detail for the Texas row. Corrected products[] to disclose this.

Quote is verbatim on NVIDIA's own site and documents a co-marketing/deployment-assistance relationship ('working with NVIDIA to help enterprises build and deploy AI factories'). It does not state that NVIDIA supplies Dell with GPUs, accelerators, or any component that Dell integrates into hardware it sells. It is a 'partner card' on a promotional page, not a supply-chain disclosure.

Quote is verbatim in Dell's 10-K and documents only that Dell has an 'AI-optimized servers' product category; it names no GPU or accelerator supplier. The research file's own gaps[] entry 'Dell AI-server supply chain (GPU supplier, assembly sites)' explicitly states this is unsourced and 'would need: Dell filing or official release naming AI-server integration sites and GPU supply agreements' -- i.e. the analyst's own gap notes contradict building this flow from these two sources. Neither party's specific role in an NVIDIA-to-Dell component flow is documented.

Quote is verbatim in src:honhai-tech-day-2024 and, read in context (the passage follows remarks by NVIDIA's Deepu Talla and Foxconn's Benjamin Ting on the NVIDIA-Foxconn AI partnership, and the release separately references the NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 platform), reasonably supports a general NVIDIA-Foxconn AI-server relationship. It does NOT name El Salto, Jalisco (or any city/state) as the location of 'the world's largest AI server factory being constructed in Mexico', and does not name NVIDIA as that factory's customer. Foxconn's own MOPS filings for El Salto give no product designation either (purpose stated only as generic '營運需求'/operational needs). Two separate, unconfirmed identifications are being stacked: (1) that El Salto is this factory, and (2) that this factory serves NVIDIA. That exceeds what 'inferred' can support under AGENTS.md (each party's role must independently be documented, only the specific link deduced) -- here Foxconn's own role at El Salto is itself undocumented.
Quote is verbatim and correctly supports only 'location' (El Salto land purchase); it makes no claim about AI servers or NVIDIA and does not, by itself, rescue the flow.

Quote ("交易總金額為美金48,850仟元") is verbatim and supports the US$48,850,000 amount. But the entity's description states specific land/building sizes (852,034 sq ft land; 324,598 sq ft plant) and asserts the size 'matches 15200 Heritage Parkway (D1)'. Neither size figure appears anywhere in this filing (which gives no acreage or building size at all), nor in any other source in this file. The filing's counterparty (PR III/CROW BUILDING E,F,G&L LP) and site are not named. This is an inference dressed as a documented fact; description corrected to remove the unsourced size figures and disclose the site link as inferred.

summary:
Systems layer (server/rack assembly, ODMs, networking) verification, 2026-09-28. 28/28 sources reached and confirmed as the stated doc_type/tier/date -- 6 SEC 10-Ks (NVIDIA, Supermicro, Dell, HPE, Arista, Celestica) via EDGAR full-text search after direct sec.gov/Archives fetches were blocked with HTTP 403 under SEC's bot policy (no headers spoofed, no bypass used; efts.sec.gov exact-phrase search confirmed every cited quote verbatim against the exact accession number in the research file); 14 Taiwan MOPS regulatory filings fetched directly by GET with the declared project User-Agent (all HTTP 200, no bypass needed); 8 company press releases/pages (NVIDIA x4, Hon Hai x2, Foxconn/WEDC, Hillwood). 99/99 evidence items checked: 93 verified verbatim as cited, 4 does_not_support, 2 verified_with_correction. 57/57 entities given an explicit verdict: 16 companies publish, 12 facilities publish, 5 facilities publish_flagged, 8 flows publish, 5 flows publish_flagged, 2 flows reject (flow:nvidia-to-dell, flow:nvidia-to-foxconn-el-salto), 7 financial_links publish, 2 financial_links publish_flagged. No entity was rejected outright (existence/location); the two rejected flows are dropped commodity-flow claims, not facility or company rejections.

Systemic problems found:
1. Wistron's two Fort Worth MOPS contracts were matched to specific street addresses by building-size proportionality rather than by anything the filings themselves state. The $110.98M 'Westport' contract is well-supported (the MOPS filing itself names the site 'Westport廠' and gives an exact 766,994 sq ft match to Hillwood's 14601 Mobility Way building) and is publish_flagged. The $48.85M 'WIUS' contract is materially weaker: that MOPS filing names neither a site nor a size at all -- it only gives an amount and counterparty, referencing an unfetched 2025-04-02 original announcement. The research file's description of that transaction stated specific land/building sizes (852,034 / 324,598 sq ft) that appear in no cited source; corrected to remove them and flag the Heritage-Parkway/D1 site link as the analyst's unconfirmed inference (fin:wistron-heritage-parkway-2025). The corresponding evidence item on fac:wistron-fort-worth was marked does_not_support for the same reason; the facility's other five evidence items are solid and it remains publish_flagged overall.
2. MOPS filings state only generic purposes ('營運需求'/operational needs, confirmed verbatim on every filing checked); every facility/financial-link description that ties a specific site to AI-server production was checked to make sure that link comes from a company release, not the MOPS filing itself. This held throughout except for the two rejected flows below.
3. Two inferred flows were rejected as unsound rather than merely flagged: flow:nvidia-to-dell (the cited NVIDIA page documents a deployment-assistance partnership, not a component-supply relationship; Dell's 10-K names no GPU supplier; the research file's own gaps[] entry already concedes this is unsourced) and flow:nvidia-to-foxconn-el-salto (stacks two unconfirmed identifications -- that El Salto is 'the' unnamed AI-server factory in Hon Hai's Tech Day release, and that its output goes to NVIDIA specifically -- exceeding what AGENTS.md's inferred-flow standard permits, since Foxconn's own role at El Salto is itself undocumented, not just the NVIDIA link). By contrast, flow:nvidia-to-supermicro-san-jose, flow:coherent-to-nvidia, and flow:nvidia-to-wistron-mobility-way were judged sound two-premise inferences with honest inference_notes and kept as publish_flagged.
4. Wistron Dallas-vs-Fort-Worth naming conflict: NVIDIA's April 2025 release verbatim says 'Wistron in Dallas'; later 2026 releases verbatim say Fort Worth. Checked that the research file does not cite the April 2025 'Dallas' quote in support of the Wistron facility's location (only in support of the Foxconn Houston facility, where 'Foxconn in Houston' from the same sentence is correct) -- the more specific, later Fort Worth documents are what the Wistron facility actually relies on. This is handled correctly; flagged in the gaps[] already and no correction was needed.
5. Foxconn Sunnyvale 'Argues' spelling: the MOPS filing verbatim reads 'East Argues Avenue' (not 'Arques', the real Sunnyvale street name). The research file's evidence quote preserves the filing's own typo verbatim and the address field separately notes the discrepancy -- correct handling, no fix needed.
6. Foxconn Houston: all three addresses (9625 Fallbrook Pines Dr.; 8228/8118 Houston Ave.; 8702-8726 Fairbanks North Houston Rd.) and all associated amounts confirmed verbatim against their MOPS filings; NVIDIA's statement that GB300 tray modules are built there confirmed verbatim in the Aug. 2026 release. This is the best-documented facility in the file.
7. Celestica Texas: the CCS-segment revenue quote is real but is company-wide, not Texas-specific; the facility's products[] list was corrected to disclose that the 10-K's property table gives no site-level product detail.

Rejected: flow:nvidia-to-dell, flow:nvidia-to-foxconn-el-salto. All companies, facilities, and financial_links were publishable (with 7 flagged for inference/attribution caveats); none required outright rejection of existence or location claims. Ran node scripts/validate.mjs systems -- see final output.
